question: What does a patient who needs verbal cues during grooming require?
explanation: Supervision involves overseeing the task and providing verbal prompts rather than physical lifting. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h1)

question: Why should nurses assess a patient's baseline ability before assisting with personal care?

options.A: To reduce the time spent writing nursing care plans
options.B: To eliminate the need for family caregiver education
options.C: To prevent the loss of remaining functional skills
options.D: To determine the hospital discharge date immediately

explanation: Allowing patients to perform tasks they are still capable of doing preserves their strength and independence. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h1)

question: Which part of the body should be washed first during a bed bath?
explanation: Washing starts from the cleanest areas, like the eyes, moving toward dirtier areas. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h2)

question: A patient with diabetes shows reduced sensation in the feet. What is the most important action during foot washing?

options.A: Soaking the feet in hot water for twenty minutes
options.B: Testing the water temperature carefully before immersion
options.C: Scrubbing the skin vigorously with a rough sponge
options.D: Applying strong antiseptic lotion between the toes

explanation: Neuropathy impairs temperature sensation, putting the patient at high risk for thermal burns. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h2)

question: What position should an unconscious patient be placed in for oral care?
explanation: A side-lying position allows fluids to drain safely from the mouth and prevents aspiration. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h3)

question: Why should removable dentures be stored in liquid overnight?

options.A: To prevent the acrylic material from warping
options.B: To dissolve stubborn food particles on the surface
options.C: To whiten the artificial teeth while resting
options.D: To kill all bacterial spores present on the plastic

explanation: Keeping dentures moist prevents them from drying out and changing shape. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h3)

question: When dressing a patient with right-sided hemiplegia, which arm goes into the shirt sleeve first?
explanation: The affected or weak side must always be dressed first. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h4)

question: What is the correct sequence when undressing a patient with a weak left arm?

options.A: Remove the sleeve from the right arm first
options.B: Cut the clothing down the front to avoid moving the arm
options.C: Pull the entire shirt over the head without using the arms
options.D: Remove the sleeve from the left arm first

explanation: Undressing starts with the unaffected side so the affected side is handled last. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h4)

question: In which direction should a nurse clean the perineal area of a female patient?
explanation: Front-to-back cleansing prevents fecal bacteria from entering the urinary tract. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of applying barrier cream to an incontinent patient's skin?

options.A: To treat underlying bacterial skin infections
options.B: To protect the skin from moisture and irritation
options.C: To mask unpleasant odors associated with urine
options.D: To speed up the healing of deep pressure ulcers

explanation: Barrier creams create a hydrophobic layer that shields the epidermis from corrosive body fluids. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h5)

question: When must a nurse perform hand hygiene during patient grooming activities?

options.B: Only when gloves appear visibly torn
options.C: At the beginning and end of the shift
options.D: Only after touching soiled bed linens

explanation: Hand hygiene must occur before and after touching a patient or their immediate environment. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h6)

question: Which action is NOT required when executing standard precautions during a bed bath?

options.A: Donning clean non-sterile gloves for perineal care
options.B: Performing hand hygiene immediately after glove removal
options.C: Properly disposing of soiled wet linens in a laundry bag
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gowns for every routine wash

explanation: Routine bed baths require clean gloves, not sterile gowns, unless splashing of body fluids is anticipated. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h6)
